items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: And these were all, of course, Claude Thornhill's selections, because he was my mentor.

ctx.x: And, of course, I always liked "The Folks Who Live On The Hill." And, of course, "Darling Nellie Gray" was more in keeping with the traditional style that he had established by doing the early "Loch Lomond" and "Annie Laurie" thing.
And these were all, of course, Claude Thornhill's selections, because he was my mentor.
In fact, while the news was getting around, Archer Winston who was a critic for one of the newspapers -- he hadn't really got into hearing Maxine Sullivan.
